analysis.title: Bonds Are "Working As Your Hedge" Again: McElligott Says Market Is Now Repricing An AI-Driven Growth Scare (Nomura note: "REPRICING THE LEFT-TAIL...FAST")
key_insights: McElligott says the market is now repricing the left side of the 2027+ US growth probability distribution because of a rethink of the AI trajectory. Two days earlier, in his "DE-TRENDED" note, he attributed the Treasury short squeeze and trend-trade unwind to positioning and crowding, not a growth scare.

Equity vol, skew and vol-of-vol ("Demand for Wings") jumped on outright hedge buying after being an afterthought in recent weeks. Spot/vol correlation has flipped back to the standard negative form (spot down, vol up).
Spot equities are accelerating through the MegaCap Tech / Nasdaq / QQQ negative-gamma flip level of about $715 in QQQ. Below that level dealers are short gamma and mechanical selling feeds on itself.
QQQ front-month implied vol rose roughly 3 points from the prior close to about 24, above the late-February curve. A month ago the front end sat around 19-20.

Nomura's rebalance projection for options dealers, levered ETFs and vol-control funds shows about $34B to sell on a further 1% drop, $134B on a 3% drop and $225B on a 5% drop. On the upside they would buy only $23.5B on a 1% bounce, and on a 5% rally vol-control selling leaves them net sellers.

Treasuries are "working as your hedge" again. Yields are at fresh one-month lows, USD rate vol is bid, and the short-term bonds-stocks correlation has reversed, so bonds are rising as AI equities sell off.

Treasury option flow was bullish: TYZ 108.5 calls, a TY week-5 105.25/105.75 strangle, FVH 106 calls, and TYZ 107.5 and 107 calls. Swaption vol on 1-month expiries of 1y and 2y tails jumped 10.1 and 11.2 on the day, while 10y-and-longer expiries barely moved, which McElligott reads as pricing Fed cuts in a growth scare.

McElligott's list of AI-rethink triggers: Anthropic ARR disappointment and IPO viability questions, Gartner's neocloud warnings, poorly received AI IPOs globally, disappointing LRCX guidance, and a capex-flattening impulse against lofty estimates. Meta kept capex full tilt and raised it, and is also doing a large equity secondary.

The triggers cut expectations for AI/hyperscaler profitability and the return to positive FCF. AI financing costs are realizing as non-linear as credit spreads widen, with more debt, loan and equity issuance coming.

Meta's 14C filing says it needs to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars" starting as early as this fall, via a new class of non-voting stock and more bonds. ZeroHedge reads this as hyperscalers selling their own upside, with credit pricing the risk that upside does not arrive.
The Semis / Energy barbell, +60% YTD on a 3 Sharpe, was hit today, with Energy -1.7% and Tech -2.9%. McElligott calls the AI Cold War constraints trade the two leaders of the S&P this year.

McElligott argues AI capex trickle-down, G10 fiscal deficits and insufficiently restrictive policy rates kept US nominal GDP running hot in a 6-10% band, which supported the earnings growth backdrop. Losing the AI capex leg weakens the earnings, run-hot and higher-for-longer rates stories together.

Counterpoint noted (Goldman Delta One's Rich Privorotsky): lower yields ease hyperscaler funding costs and could eventually put a floor under the AI trade. ZeroHedge sides with the left tail and says the bond market is late to the move.

market_movers.rationale: Meta kept capex full tilt and raised it, and is running a large equity secondary. Its 14C filing says it needs hundreds of billions of dollars in new financing, which McElligott frames as hyperscalers selling calls on themselves.
Guidance disappointed against elevated whispers, one of the items on McElligott's AI-rethink list.
QQQ is breaking through the roughly $715 negative-gamma flip level. Nomura projects $134B of mechanical selling on a 3% drop and $225B on a 5% drop.

sector_views.rationale: Tech fell 2.9% on the day as the AI trajectory rethink hit hyperscaler profitability and FCF expectations.
Energy fell 1.7% on the day as the Semis / Energy barbell, +60% YTD, unwound.

earnings_insights: Lam Research (LRCX) guidance disappointed against elevated whispers overnight. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
Meta kept capex full tilt and raised it versus prior expectations (no figures given), and is pushing ahead with a large equity secondary.

macro_indicators.interpretation: McElligott says nominal GDP has been running hot, helped by AI capex trickle-down and fiscal deficits, and this supported the earnings growth backdrop. The loss of the AI capex leg threatens that.
Yields fell as bonds regained their role as a hedge against equity risk.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Front-end rate vol is moving while 10y-and-longer expiries barely moved, so the market is pricing near-term Fed policy, meaning cuts in a growth scare.

risk_factors: Further AI-trajectory disappointments, including ARR misses, weak IPO reception and capex-flattening concerns.
AI financing costs are non-linear, with credit spreads widening and large debt, loan and equity supply coming, including Meta's planned raise of hundreds of billions of dollars.
Dealer short-gamma feedback below QQQ $715, with $134B of selling on a 3% drop and $225B on a 5% drop.
A growth scare in 2027+ US growth hits the nominal GDP and earnings backdrop that AI capex trickle-down had supported.
Competition for capital: Meta, Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI are all raising from the same investors.

Skew and vol-of-vol are rising on outright hedge buying after weeks when demand was only for upside calls.

Dealer, levered ETF and vol-control rebalance: sell $34B on -1%, $134B on -3%, $225B on -5%. Buy $23.5B on +1%, and net sellers on a +5% rally.
Hedge flow: SPX Jan 5900 puts paid 18.3 on 1,300 contracts. VIX Nov 25 calls, 18,150 committed at 0.85. SPX Dec 7400 puts (25-delta, tied to 7730), 2,000 bought at $84.50.

Treasury option flow: TYZ 108.5 calls paid 6 on 49,999. TY week-5 105.25/105.75 strangle paid 36-37 on 20,000. FVH 106 calls paid up to 27 on 15,000, then another 20,000. TYZ 107.5 and 107 calls traded 23,000 and 17,000.
Swaption vol on 1-month expiries of 1y and 2y tails rose 10.1 and 11.2 on the day. 10y-and-longer expiries barely moved.
The semis/energy barbell, +60% YTD on a 3 Sharpe, unwound on the day, with Energy -1.7% and Tech -2.9%. The "High Sharpe" trend trades were blown up two days earlier by the Treasury short squeeze.
geopolitical: McElligott calls Tech and Energy the two legs of the "Core Constraints of the AI Cold War".
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Delta One desk (Rich Privorotsky) explained why AI's pain is the bond market's gain, and described a reflexive loop in which lower yields ease hyperscaler funding costs and could eventually put a floor under the AI trade.
Echoing virtually every other desk today, McElligott pins the move on the AI Trajectory Rethink.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Delta One desk describes a reflexive loop in which lower yields ease hyperscaler funding costs and could eventually put a floor under the AI trade.
tension_points.bear_case: The floor exists only because the market is pricing less AI growth, and Meta alone needs hundreds of billions of dollars from the same investors that Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI are also tapping. Dealers are short gamma below QQQ $715, with $225B of mechanical selling on a 5% drop.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break lower through QQQ $715 with further hyperscaler financing or ARR disappointments would show the left tail is dominant.
